answer: Give every applicant one hive staked to one meadow vertex in the registry. At the zenith of bloom the holder draws nectar only after the lab countersigns the pollen-DNA profile of the prior draw, so each draw is gated on the last and one hive can never stand for two holders. A copied profile is caught: every meadow's pollen blend is distinct and shifts with the season, so a replay never matches the lab's fresh sample. Keeping one hive costs $470 plus 29 hours; 5,000 identities would need 5,000 hives, $2,350,000, and 145,000 hours, because no bulk purchase reproduces a meadow's pollen blend.
